messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a decision on where to surface deployment-level behaviors (routing/eviction/telemetry toggles) in the public API vs keeping them internal. TL;DR: fine-grained per-deploy API vs coarse per-tenant flags. Thoughts?

jonathan: I lean coarse. Simpler contract, fewer breaking changes for customers. Expose a small set: capacity-tier, region-preference, fallback-model. Keep advanced knobs internal for runtime and console.

sara: Coarse is safer short term but it hurts Dedicated/Private use cases where customers need strict pinning/eviction controls. We should offer an advanced surface (opt-in) for Dedicated/Private customers.

kevin: If we add an opt-in advanced surface we need strong auth + audit trails. Also versioned API paths so hosted customers can't accidentally call private-only APIs. :thinking:

maria: Proposal: keep /v1/public minimal (tenant-level) and add /v1/deployments/{deploy_id}/config for Dedicated/Private with RBAC. For Hosted, calls to that endpoint return 403 unless tenant has 'advanced-deploy' enabled. Document explicit fallback semantics.

jonathan: How about a feature-flag-driven rollout? Start with docs + console behind a feature flag, then SDK support. Add a deprecation window for any overlapping semantics so integrators have time.

sara: Important: routing precedence must be deterministic. Proposal: precedence = per-deploy override > tenant-level setting > system default. Also emit a telemetry tag ("override_applied") so we can audit which rule won.

kevin: Caching/batching note: per-deploy KV cache keys must include deploy_id when deploy-level overrides are active, otherwise requests could get pooled incorrectly. That has perf/memory impact. Possible compromise: include deploy_id in key only when an override exists.

maria: Implementation note: runtime change = add deploy_id tag on the request context and on batching key only for deployments with overrides enabled. Router must propagate deploy_id from API layer to runtime.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: FYI — quick smoke test: passing header `x-deploy-id` is backward compatible and shows up in traces as `deploy.id`.

sara: Migration plan (rough): 1) publish API shape + docs; 2) Console + SDK opt-in; 3) runtime flags for batching/caching behavior; 4) 3-week canary in Dedicated; 5) telemetry dashboard tracking "override_applied" ratio and cache-key split. I'll draft the RFC with API examples.

jonathan: +1. Add billing check: if deploy pins a larger model, cost attribution must go to the deploy owner. Ensure billing tags flow through router.

maria: I'll synthesize and draft the RFC. Action items: @sara to write initial draft, @kevin to enumerate runtime changes (batching, cache keys, trace tags), @jonathan to outline rollout & billing checks. Ping me when ready. :thumbsup:

sara: I'll start the draft this afternoon and include a minimal API example. Example snippet we'll include in RFC:
```
PATCH /v1/deployments/123/config
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-ggml-medium",
  "fallback_model": "redwood-ggml-small",
  "eviction_policy": "pin",
  "billing_tag": "project-xyz"
}
```

maria: Perfect — thanks. Keep it focused on the host/dedicated/private boundary and explicit permission checks. We'll reconvene after the draft.
